hypothesis: If Thompson is right, in a molecular species-level mammal phylogeny Perissodactyla share a more recent common ancestor with Lagomorpha than with any other ungulate order (Artiodactyla, Cetacea, Proboscidea, Sirenia, Hyracoidea), and Lagomorpha share a more recent common ancestor with Perissodactyla than with Rodentia.
pass_criterion: In the Upham et al. 2019 maximum clade credibility tree and at least 95% of the posterior credible trees sampled, the MRCA age of (Perissodactyla + Lagomorpha) is younger than the MRCA age of (Perissodactyla + Artiodactyla/Cetacea) and of (Perissodactyla + each of Proboscidea, Sirenia, Hyracoidea), AND younger than the MRCA age of (Lagomorpha + Rodentia). Both conditions must hold in at least 95% of sampled trees.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if, in the MCC tree or in more than 5% of sampled trees, Perissodactyla's MRCA with Artiodactyla/Cetacea is younger than its MRCA with Lagomorpha, or Lagomorpha's MRCA with Rodentia is younger than its MRCA with Perissodactyla. Expected under the current consensus: Perissodactyla fall in Laurasiatheria and Lagomorpha fall in Euarchontoglires with Rodentia (Glires), so the claim is refuted.
interpretation: Thompson's "more closely related" is read as recency of common ancestry, i.e. relative node ages and clade membership on a phylogeny, not skull-shape similarity. His Perissodactyla maps to the order Perissodactyla, Leporidae to Lagomorpha (the dataset has Leporidae species), Ungulates to the traditional hoofed orders (Artiodactyla, Cetacea, Proboscidea, Sirenia, Hyracoidea), and Rodentia to the order Rodentia. The modern reinterpretation is that the inference comes from molecular phylogenetics, which is independent of the transformation-grid morphology that Thompson used. Use the tip taxonomy in Data_S1 to assign species to orders. Compute node ages from the MCC trees in Data_S5 and from the credible tree sets in Data_S7.

dataset.name: Inferring the mammal tree: Species-level sets of phylogenies for questions in ecology, evolution, and conservation
dataset.why_it_fits: It provides a dated species-level phylogeny of about 6,000 mammals, with an MCC tree (Data_S5) and sets of credible trees (Data_S7). Both the master taxonomy (Data_S1) and the trees allow computing MRCA ages for Perissodactyla, Lagomorpha, Rodentia and the other ungulate orders.
